newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen shares move up at noon on bank dividend.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares move up at noon on bank dividend.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B share indices rose at midday on Wednesday, due to market heavyweight Shenzhen Development Bank Ltd's announcement of an attractive dividend plan for 1996, brokers said.
The Chinese yuan-based A share index firmed 7.86 points or 1.86 percent to 430.26 points on turnover of 3.3 billion yuan.
The hard currency B share index jumped 2.26 points or 1.71 percent to 134.36 on turnover of HK$17 million.
"The markets rose because Development Bank's dividend is unchanged," an analyst at Central-South Securities said.
The bank announced on Wednesday that its shareholders had approved a five-for-10 bonus issue plus a pre-tax cash payout of 0.2 yuan per share as 1996 dividend.
Investors had feared the bank would adjust the dividend plan, which was drafted before the company was punished by securities regulators for trading its own shares, brokers said.
Beijing last month confiscated the bank's illicit profits of 90.34 million yuan from the stock trading and sacked the bank's former president He Yun for the scandal.
Trading in the bank's A shares was suspended on Tuesday for the shareholders meeting and the Shenzhen bourse said it would resume on Wednesday afternoon.
The issue closed at 36.71 yuan on Monday.
But brokers said they expected the bank to put in a mediocre performance on Wednesday afternoon because of it had forecast lower earnings rise for 1997.

The bank expected pre-tax profits to rise about nine percent year-on-year to 1.0 billion yuan in 1997, the Shenzhen-based Securities Times on Wednesday quoted the bank's chairman Xu Jicai as saying. He did not issue a net profit forecast.
The forecast came after the bank posted a net 1996 profit of 787.48 million yuan against 435.13 million in 1995.
"Despite the intact dividend, the bank share is likely to ease on resumption of trading in the afternoon because of the disappointing forecast," an analyst said.
In the A share market, First Automobile was the most actively traded on volume of 8.4 million shares, rising 0.84 yuan to 11.30 yuan.
In the B share market, Shenzhen SEZ Real Estate was the biggest gainer, surging HK$0.25 or 9.36 percent to HK$2.92. But volume was a thin 6,600 shares.
